Written 2026-09-15 by a read-only contract agent. Every number below was re-read today by SELECT (Supabase flawuiqbvjobmkfkauhw), by get_edge_function (soccer-grid-validate v23, updated 2026-09-07, repo copy sha256 6aad2815... equals scripts/data/edgeDeployed.json) or by a 24h log read. No edge function was invoked. Probe SQL: C:\Users\antho\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\r613\probe_contract_2026-09-15.sql plus the earlier probe_routes.mjs, probe_wc_match.mjs and probe_queries.sql in the same folder.

DECISION ON THE COLLEGE GRID PRECEDENT: fix the records pass now; do not move Soccer Grid to a browser key this round.
1. Soccer Grid finishes and College Grid did not. game_completions for soccer-grid: 86 since 2026-07-01 (52 at 900 or more), 72 since fail closed on 07-22, 31 since 08-30. College Grid had 2 rows since 07-22. The default normal tier had no AI cell on 46 of 46 daily boards (08-01 to 09-15), and since 08-30 the correct picks split normal 360, hard 40, easy 9.
2. What is broken is five rules inside one 440 line function, not the architecture. Every proven wrong verdict traces to them: substring clubs (Taarabt confirmed at Rangers from a QPR row), the Atlético alias gap (6 wrong cached refusals), nationality fallthrough (4 caps refusals), substring World Cup names (Cristiano Ronaldo and Thomas Müller cached as 1994 winners, "ram", "pirl", "stefa" cached YES), and cross-person pairing (Romário x 1994 x Defender, Ruggeri and Frank fullNames).
3. A browser judge needs definite NOs the tables do not hold. Clubs fill 1,888 of 4,260 slots and no table holds complete careers (stints is player_market_values capped at rank 500 per position per year; Defensive Midfield has 0 player-years in 2023 to 2025). Positions fill 986 slots and settle NO for only about 2,500 names (audit). Leagues fill 474 slots, 441 of them on easy boards, with no club-season-league table. 42 honour labels (74 slots) have no per-player data. Judged without the model, a wrong club or position guess would be a free retry on most cells, so boards could be won but almost never lost.
4. Size. Retiring league labels alone touches 372 of the 710 boards, and regenerating boards resets rarity (soccer_grid_selections is keyed by puzzle_id). The key would sit over 80,586 stint rows (27,803 names) plus 9,427 squad rows, against the NFL key's 22,008 rows. That is two or three rounds, not one.
5. Revisit when a club-season-league table is imported and a second position source covers the position slots, or if the model allowance is withdrawn for good.

GOAL. Every verdict the records pass gives is either a confirmed fact about one person or a definite NO from a complete fact (a complete World Cup winning squad, or a single stored nationality that a second table does not contradict). A club miss is never a NO. No label reaches a matcher that was not built for it. The model stays as the fail closed fallback for what records cannot settle.

What does not change: the hook (src/hooks/useSoccerGrid.ts), the page, the boards, tiers, the cache-first order, the rate limit, the prompt, the Round 407 and 501 name guard, the 429 handling and every unverified shape. No src file changes, so no snapshot changes.

1. DATA: GENERATED IDENTITY (derived, never typed)
New scripts/genSoccerGridIds.mjs. Reads through REST with the publishable key (paged, retried like simSoccerGridLabels.getPage): soccer_player_club_stints (club, name_folded, player_name, first_year, last_year, nationality), world_cup_players (player_name, club, nationality, world_cup_year), soccer_club_puzzles (full_name, common_names), soccer_grid_puzzles (rows_json, cols_json) and the labels of the 15 fallback puzzles in src/data/soccerGridPuzzles.ts. Writes two things, and --check exits 1 when either differs from a fresh derivation:
 a) scripts/data/soccerGridIds.json: per label, the resolved stored strings, the evidence behind each (exact label, exact puzzle full_name, or world_cup_players n/total), names reachable, and every unresolved or low coverage label with its reason. Header names the command, the thresholds and the date.
 b) the block between the lines "// @generated-ids-begin" and "// @generated-ids-end" inside supabase/functions/soccer-grid-validate/index.ts: CLUB_IDS (folded label text after "Played for " to exact stored strings), CLUB_COMPOUND (label to {mode: both or either, parts}), NATION_IDS (folded label to {label, stints, wc[]}). Do not edit the block by hand.
Club rules, in this order, per label or compound part:
 - Names of the label: the label itself, plus the full_name of the single soccer_club_puzzles row whose full_name or common_names fold equal to the label. Two or more rows means ambiguous: resolve nothing. Common names are only used to find the row, never matched against stints themselves.
 - A stored string (stints club split on " / ") is accepted when its fold equals one of the names, or when a world_cup_players club spelling whose fold equals one of the names co-occurs with that stored string for the same folded player name with first_year <= world cup year and last_year >= year minus 1, on at least 3 players and at least 0.3 of that spelling's joined players. Rows whose stored club contains " / " are excluded from the co-occurrence count.
 - Compound labels: "both A and B" and "A or B" are split and each part resolved as above. A label with an unresolved part is unresolved.
 - No hand alias. The five v23 CLUB_ALIASES entries re-derive: PSG via the puzzle row (Paris Saint-Germain), Bayer Leverkusen 25/36, Celta Vigo 7/8, Rennes 19/32, LA Galaxy 4/8.
 - Reading today: 101 single labels, 99 resolve; unresolved Santos (two puzzle rows: Santos FC, Santos Laguna, 16 slots) and "England at a World Cup" (1 slot); low coverage Grêmio (only the 1 name stored as "Grêmio"; the 166 names at "Grêmio Foot-Ball Porto Alegrense" have no evidence at threshold, 17 slots); "both AC Milan and Inter" unresolved because "Inter" names two puzzle rows (1 slot); Man United and Man City, Real Madrid and Atlético, Boca or River all resolve. No world_cup_players spelling maps to two targets. Examples: "Atlético Madrid" and "Atletico Madrid" give Atlético de Madrid (180 names, evidence 35/52) plus Atlético Madrid (1); "Barcelona" gives FC Barcelona (48/76) plus Barcelona; "Rangers" gives Rangers FC only (8/10); "Tottenham" gives Tottenham Hotspur via the puzzle row.
Nation rules:
 - The only typed input is a language table DEMONYM moved out of the function into the generator (label word to English country name), extended so every nationality label on the boards has a key: add "south korean" to south korea and "tunisian" to tunisia. A label is nationality only when its fold is a DEMONYM key.
 - Country to stored stints string: fold equality, else token set equality ("south korea" and "Korea, South"), else a world_cup_players nationality spelling equal to the country that co-occurs with one stints nationality on at least 3 players and at least 0.9 share (today: Ivory Coast to Cote d'Ivoire 59/59, Turkey to Türkiye 21/21, Bosnia and Herzegovina to Bosnia-Herzegovina 29/29). wc[] lists the world_cup_players spellings seen for that stints string.
 - Reading today: 37 nationality labels. Irish is Ireland (196 names, not Northern Ireland 68), Nigerian is Nigeria (248, not Niger 6), Ivorian is Cote d'Ivoire (221), South Korean is Korea, South (175). "African" has no DEMONYM key and is not a nationality.

2. VALIDATOR v24 (supabase/functions/soccer-grid-validate/index.ts)
Structure. All judging moves into pure functions between the lines "// @judge-begin" and "// @judge-end" (the generated block sits inside it). The block has no import, no fetch, no sb, no Deno. serve() does the reads and calls judge(). Delete from the file: DEMONYM, CLUB_ALIASES, clubMatches' substring test, parseCriterion's regex fallthrough, careerComplete and the v23 checkWorldCupWinner matcher. Keep: norm, TRANSLIT, cacheKeyOf, WC_WINNER_BY_YEAR, positionBucket, the stints lookup on name_folded (eq, then the unique surname like fallback), the rate limiter, the whole AI branch verbatim.
Closed classifier, first match wins:
 1. /^(\d{4}) World Cup Winner$/ with the year in WC_WINNER_BY_YEAR: wc_winner.
 2. Fold equals one of "forward fwd", "midfielder mid", "defender def", "goalkeeper gk": position.
 3. /^Played for (.+)$/: fold of the rest in CLUB_IDS is club, in CLUB_COMPOUND is compound, otherwise other.
 4. /^Played in /: league.
 5. Fold in NATION_IDS: nationality.
 6. Everything else: other.
 league and other never produce a records verdict. Reading today over 236 labels and 4,260 slots: club 99 labels / 1,867 slots, compound 3 / 3, nationality 37 / 471, position 4 / 986, wc_winner 11 / 338, league 12 / 474, other 70 / 121 (18 club shaped unresolved slots, the 25 labels v23 sent to the nationality matcher with 29 slots, 42 honour labels with 74 slots).
Records criteria per stints row r:
 - club: some trimmed part of r.club split on " / " is exactly one of CLUB_IDS strings. A miss is "unknown", never false.
 - compound either: any part matches on some row; miss unknown. Compound both: every part matches on some row and the fetched rows carry one nationality; otherwise unknown.
 - position: positionBucket(r.position) is the bucket; miss unknown (as v23).
 - nationality: r.nationality equals NATION_IDS.stints. A definite false only when all four hold: the name resolved by the exact folded full name (not the surname fallback); every fetched row carries one nationality; it is not the wanted string; and no world_cup_players row whose player_name equals the stored stints player_name exactly has a nationality in NATION_IDS.wc (one extra read, made only when a nationality false is about to be returned). Otherwise unknown.
Pairing two records criteria: YES only when one single stints row satisfies both (the Round 482 same-row rule from validate-player). Compound both counts as satisfied for the name, then the paired criterion needs any row.
World Cup names (squad query adds date_of_birth and nationality). Fold everything with norm; nospace means spaces removed. For the typed guess g against the year's squad rows s, first band that applies:
 A. g equals s, or nospace(g) equals nospace(s): YES on that row.
 B. every token of g is a whole token of s, or nospace(g) equals one token of s, and exactly one squad row qualifies: YES on that row. Two or more rows qualify: unknown.
 D. every token of some s is a token of g and g has extra tokens: unknown.
 E. near: g shares at least one whole token with some s; or nospace(g), at least 3 characters, is a prefix of a token of s or of nospace(s); or Levenshtein(nospace(g), nospace(s)) <= max(1, floor(maxlen / 6)); or some token pair of length at least 4 is within Levenshtein 1: unknown.
 F. otherwise: definite false (the squad is complete, 15 or more rows required as today).
 Measured on today's cache: data YES rows on these labels split A 67, B 30, D 4 (cristiano ronaldo 1994, thomas muller 1994, ronaldo nazario 1994 and 2002, xavi hernandez 2010), E 3 (ram, pirl, stefa); data NO rows split E 22 (tafarel, ronaldino, jairzinio, lillian thuram, sweinsteiger, umtitti, voler, mathaus, blaise matiudi, julian alavrez, jurgen koller, ricardino, beberto, mcallister and 8 correct refusals near a squad name) and F 137.
Pairing with a World Cup YES on squad row R:
 - position: YES when positionBucket(R.position) is the bucket, else unknown.
 - club, compound or nationality from stints: counted only when norm(stints player_name) equals norm(R.player_name) and |(debut_year minus debut_age) minus year(R.date_of_birth)| <= 2; otherwise unknown. (Romário: stints born 1993, squad 1966.)
 - both labels World Cup years: YES only when the two matched rows share folded name and date_of_birth.
 - properName is always R.player_name.
Verdict writing: a pair is YES when both criteria are true, false when either is false, otherwise the AI branch runs exactly as in v23. Reasons keep their exact v23 wording ("Verified from career records." and `${shown} does not satisfy "${which}".`). Every verdict object this version caches, records or AI, gains rule: "v24" (the hook reads only valid, fullName, unverified, exhausted). The header comment is rewritten to describe v24 and its date.
Deploy and sync: run genSoccerGridIds.mjs (writes the block), run the harnesses, then deploy through the Supabase MCP deploy_edge_function with the repo index.ts. Read it back with get_edge_function: version 24, and the CRLF normalised sha256 of the returned content equals the repo file. Update scripts/data/edgeDeployed.json soccer-grid-validate to that sha256, version 24 and the deploy date in the same commit. simEdgeSync's unverified baseline stays 19.

3. BOARDS AND LABELS: none retired or regenerated this round

4. CACHE PURGE (right after the v24 read-back, same session; the cache is served before the records pass)

 select 'P1 club data refusal' why, cache_key from c where verdict->>'reason' like '% does not satisfy "Played for %'

   delete from ai_validation_cache a using r613_purge p where a.game = 'soccer-grid' and a.cache_key = p.cache_key and not (a.verdict ? 'rule');

5. HARNESSES

risks: More model load. Club misses (64 distinct cached refusals in 62 days), the World Cup D and E bands (30 rows in 33 days) and the 25 labels v23 sent to the nationality matcher all go to the model now. After the free allowance runs out (15:59Z on 2026-09-14, 7 day-429 lines in 24h), those guesses are free retries, so easy boards made of club, league and position labels can rarely be lost late in the day. Same-nationality namesakes can still merge for compound labels: player_market_values holds 338 single-nationality names spanning more than one birth year cluster. The same-row rule covers club x position pairs but not both-club labels (1 hard board).

The cache is read before the records pass. Every verdict the purge targets keeps being served until step 4 runs, and v23 rows written between the export and the deploy are missed unless the export is taken after the read-back (the rule marker guard assumes that order).

The replay reads stints and squads at replay time. A table import between replay and delete changes the list; the DO block raises and rolls back on a count mismatch, and the builder must then redo steps 1 to 3.

The near band is wide on purpose. It sends some correct refusals to the model (Carlos Alberto x 2002, Roberto Baggio x 2002, Ronaldinho x 1994, Inesta x 2006 in today's cache), costing allowance, not correctness. A narrower band would bring back hard refusals of misspellings.
